statements.worth_reason: The headline's "128GB 4-card configuration costs less than $3800" is a media value framing of a niche Intel workstation card; it carries no business scale and cannot change any NVIDIA revenue, margin or share answer.

Intel's standing $950 reference price for the Arc Pro B70 is a product price with no change, no volume and no NVIDIA business it competes for at scale; it is a product detail without business scale (section 5.3 row 1).

A Puget Systems decode benchmark (RTX 5090 4-5x faster, 1792 vs 608 GB/s) is a consumer-card benchmark detail that only confirms NVIDIA's known bandwidth lead; it touches no revenue, margin or competitive-position answer.

missed.quote: It also happens to be one of the most expensive GPUs retail consumers can buy in 2026, going for as much as two times its stated MSRP of $2,000 for the Founders Edition at launch, leaving many cost-sensitive AI builders turning to older Nvidia GPUs equipped with 24GB of VRAM such as the RTX 4090, 3090Ti and 3090.
missed.why: The only NVIDIA-specific datum in the piece: RTX 5090 street prices up to 2x MSRP, tied by the article to the DRAM crisis, is a small signal of gaming-GPU supply tightness; gaming is a minor segment and the channel, not NVIDIA, captures the premium, so it is low weight.

grade_reason: Every kept record is noise (a competitor workstation-card price, its headline restatement, and a consumer benchmark), one duplicates another, and the one NVIDIA-relevant line (5090 street price at up to 2x MSRP) is not kept; the page should have yielded at most one low-weight record.
standard_doubt: Section 5.3 row 1 boundary ("对手拿它和本公司产品比的说法不能用这一行删掉，按 5.1 判（Alex 判 4：AMD 2.4 倍是辅助）") read literally pushes the Puget Systems comparison of the RTX 5090 against four Arc Pro B70 cards into 'keep as auxiliary'; the AMD precedent was a competitor's data-centre claim against NVIDIA's core product, while this is a third-party consumer benchmark NVIDIA wins, and an analyst would not note it. The boundary should be limited to comparisons that bear on a contested market.
